method: Each key below was DISCOVERED, not written from memory: one read-only GET of https://api.gbif.org/v1/species/match?name=<name>&rank=<rank>&kingdom=Animalia on the discovery date, taking usageKey, rank, status, matchType and confidence from the answer. Only matches with matchType EXACT, status ACCEPTED and the expected rank were kept. The keys are GBIF backbone keys; a search by taxonKey includes the taxon's descendants.
backbone_note: GBIF backbone keys can change when the backbone is rebuilt. Re-run the discovery (see docs/external_context.md section 7) and compare before trusting this file after a long time; the loader refuses a file whose groups do not satisfy the rules in oah.external.taxa.
selection_note: The selection is the project's own judgement, not a regulatory or official list: the orders whose larvae are the classic freshwater macroinvertebrate indicator groups (Ephemeroptera, Plecoptera, Trichoptera, together called EPT), and four more groups that are common in freshwater macroinvertebrate surveys or are freshwater specialists. Presence of a group near a site says nothing about the water quality of the site.

groups.name: Ephemeroptera
groups.justification: EPT order: larvae live in freshwater and are a standard macroinvertebrate indicator group.
groups.caveat: Records of adults (winged stages) show where animals were seen, not necessarily where the larvae live.

groups.name: Plecoptera
groups.justification: EPT order: larvae live in freshwater and are a standard macroinvertebrate indicator group.
groups.caveat: Records of adults show where animals were seen, not necessarily where the larvae live.

groups.name: Trichoptera
groups.justification: EPT order: larvae live in freshwater and are a standard macroinvertebrate indicator group.
groups.caveat: Records of adults show where animals were seen, not necessarily where the larvae live.

groups.name: Odonata
groups.justification: Larvae are aquatic predators of freshwater; adults are conspicuous and widely recorded by citizen scientists.
groups.caveat: Many records are of adults, which can be far from water.

groups.name: Chironomidae
groups.justification: A family of mostly aquatic larvae found in almost every freshwater habitat and common in macroinvertebrate surveys.
groups.caveat: The family is large and ecologically varied, so a record says little about a particular habitat.

groups.name: Gammaridae
groups.justification: Amphipod crustaceans of fresh and brackish water, common in macroinvertebrate surveys.
groups.caveat: The family also contains brackish and marine species, so a record is not necessarily from freshwater.

groups.name: Unionida
groups.justification: Freshwater bivalves that live in rivers and lakes.
groups.caveat: Records can come from old surveys and museum specimens as well as recent observations.
